title: The proper Hilbert presheaf of an algebraic-space morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $a:A\to B$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the scheme tests $T\to B$, sheaf fibres $A_T$, projections, and finite-presentation and morphism-property conventions of [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Define $\mathcal H_{A/B}(T)$ to be the subset of closed-subspace classes $C$ of $A_T$ [def-sfb-space-closed-subspace] such that $C\to T$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation. The transition for every scheme map $h:T\prime\to T$ over $B$ is inverse image of the closed subspace along $A_{T\prime}\to A_T$: it is the unique closed-subspace class whose inclusion forms a cartesian square with the original inclusion. Base change preserves the three properties, and uniqueness gives identity and composition laws. This defines a set-valued presheaf on schemes over $B$, without a finite-degree, finite-fibre, flat-base-change or Noetherian restriction.
